issues.span: "I have arisen."
issues.evidence: Tibetan "བདག་ནི་མཉམ་པར་བཞག་ཅེའམ་ལངས་" (Skt vyutthita): "ལངས" means rising up out of equipoise; bo-mipham 1-10 glosses it "དེ་ལས་ལངས་སོ" (I have risen from it). "I have arisen" can be read as "I have come into being".
issues.fix: "I am in meditative equipoise," or "I have risen from it."

issues.span: conjures an emanation at a crossroads, / And cuts off the tens of millions of heads of a large crowd of people
issues.evidence: Tibetan "བཞི་མདོར་སྤྲུལ་བྱས་ཏེ། སྐྱེ་བོ་ཕལ་ཆེན་མགོ་མང་...གཅོད་" and Skt nirmiṇitvā...mahato janasya: the large crowd that is beheaded is itself the conjured emanation. bo-rangjung 1-18: "སྐྱེ་བོའི་ཚོགས་ཆེན་པོ་སྤྲུལ་པར་བྱས་ཏེ" (conjures a great crowd of people). The English singular "an emanation" and a separate "large crowd of people" lets the victims be read as real people, which blurs the point of the analogy ("those to be killed" are illusions).
issues.fix: conjures a large crowd of people as emanations at a crossroads, / And cuts off the many millions of heads of that crowd

issues.span: [Mipham, Khenrab and the Sanskrit read: a fire that has gone out]
issues.evidence: The Tibetan root reads "དཔེར་ན་མི་ཤི་" (a dead person), which the English already renders. The bracketed variant-reading note is not in the Tibetan and sits inside the verse text (bo-mipham and bo-khenrab 1-21 read "མེ་ཤི"; bo-rangjung reads "མི་ཤི"); it is a philological note, not part of the translation.
issues.fix: Remove the bracket from the verse line and move it to a note: "For example, just as a dead person has nowhere to go,"

issues.span: Pratyekabuddhas reach the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and those of sharp faculties reach the awakening of a Buddha.
issues.evidence: Tibetan line 4 "རང་རྒྱལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་དང་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་བྱང་ཆུབ་རེག" has no stated subject; it names two awakenings that are reached. Making "Pratyekabuddhas" the subject is circular (those who already are pratyekabuddhas reaching pratyekabuddha awakening). bo-mipham 2-32 and bo-khenrab 2-32 supply the subjects as beings of middling faculties ("དབང་པོ་འབྲིང") and of sharp faculties ("དབང་པོ་རྣོན་པོ").
issues.fix: those of middling faculties reach the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and those of sharp faculties reach the awakening of a Buddha.

issues.evidence: Line 2 has a second ཡོངས་བསྔོ (“བྱང་ཆུབ་འདུ་ཤེས་ཡོངས་བསྔོ་སེམས་ཅན་འདུ་ཤེས”); bo-mipham 2-42 glosses it as the perception attached to the object of dedication (“ཡོངས་སུ་བསྔོ་ཡུལ་གྱི་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་འདུ་ཤེས”) and awakening as the basis of dedication (“བསྔོ་བའི་གནས་བྱང་ཆུབ”). The English renders ཡོངས་བསྔོ only once, in line 1.
issues.fix: And if there is the perception of awakening [as that to which one dedicates] and the perception of sentient beings [as those for whom one dedicates]

issues.span: bodhisattva seeking awakening
issues.evidence: Tibetan has only བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ (locked: bodhisattva); “seeking awakening” is an added gloss (bo-mipham 2-50: “བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དམིགས་པ་ཅན”).
issues.fix: Such a bodhisattva

issues.span: many billions of sentient beings
issues.evidence: Tibetan “ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་མང་” (many ཁྲག་ཁྲིག, niyuta; bo-mipham 2-50 “ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་མང་པོ”); the same number is rendered “hundreds of billions” elsewhere in this batch (2-39, 2-47), so “billions” understates and is inconsistent.
issues.fix: many hundreds of billions of sentient beings

issues.span: those fully entered into supreme awakening
issues.evidence: བྱང་ཆུབ་དམ་པར་རབ་ཞུགས = those who have set out/engaged on the path to supreme awakening (bo-khenrab 4-6: “བྱང་ཆུབ་དམ་པར་རབ་ཏུ་ཞུགས་པ”, who gradually enter through hearing/reflecting/meditating). “Entered into awakening” can be read as having attained it, which the last line (they will touch awakening before long) excludes.
issues.fix: those who have fully set out toward supreme awakening

issues.span: Felt little inclination, thinking
issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཐུགས་ཁྲལ་ཆུང་བར་མཛད" (little concern/exertion); bo-mipham 4-48 states the object: "ཆོས་སྟོན་པ་ལ་ཐུགས་ཁྲལ་ཆུང་བར་མཛད" (little concern for teaching the Dharma); Sanskrit "alpotsuko". The English leaves open what he was disinclined toward.
issues.fix: Felt little inclination to teach, thinking, "Who among the masses of sentient beings will understand?"

issues.span: Endowed with skillful means, must apply themselves to the perfection of wisdom; / Without this wisdom, the mother of the Guides, they will not attain it.
issues.evidence: The Tibetan given has three lines (ending "ཐབས་དང་ལྡན་པས་ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་འདྲེན་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་མེད་ན་ཐོབ་པར་འགྱུར་མ་ཡིན"), with the words "ཕ[་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པ]" and "ཡུམ" not fully written; the English has four lines and supplies "perfection of wisdom" and "mother" from the Sanskrit pāda division and from bo-mipham 4-52 ("འདྲེན་པ་རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡུམ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕར་ཕྱིན") and bo-khenrab 4-52. Line count differs from the Tibetan, and the supplied words are not marked as supplied.
issues.fix: Endowed with skillful means, one must apply oneself to the [perfection of] wisdom; without this wisdom, [the mother] of the Guides, it will not be attained.

issues.span: when thoroughly questioned about their conduct and faculties,
issues.evidence: Tibetan "སྤྱོད་པ་དང་ནི་དབང་པོ་ཡོངས་དྲིས་ལ" has an unstated questioner; the questions concern the conduct and faculties of the irreversible (bo-mipham 4-98: someone asks "བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གང་ལ ... སྤྱོད་པ་ཇི་ལྟ་བུ་ཡིན་པ་དང་ ... དབང་པོ ... ཡོངས་སུ་དྲིས་པ་ལ"; bo-rangjung 4-98: asked about the irreversible's conduct, faculties and signs). The English participle attaches to the bodhisattva ("a bodhisattva ... questioned about their conduct"), suggesting he is asked about his own conduct.
issues.fix: If, when someone thoroughly asks about conduct and faculties, a bodhisattva does not fully teach the Dharma of emptiness and signlessness,

issues.span: Sentient beings, fully conceptualizing, desire food,
issues.evidence: The Tibetan as given reads "སེམས་ཅན་ཡོངས་སུ་ལྟོགས་པ་ཟས་ལ་འདོད་བྱེད" (ལྟོགས་པ = hungry, "utterly hungry"). The English follows the reading "ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོག་པ/རྟོགས་པ" (conceptualizing) found in bo-mipham 5-16, bo-rangjung 5-16, bo-khenrab 5-16 and Sanskrit "parikalpayamāna". The departure from the Tibetan wording is not flagged.
issues.fix: Sentient beings, fully conceptualizing [Tib. text: "utterly hungry"], desire food,

issues.span: In this, there is nothing that becomes afflicted or completely pure, / And the bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
issues.evidence: Tibetan "འདི་ལ་གང་ཡང་ཉོན་མོངས་རྣམ་དག་འགྱུར་མེད་པར། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔས ... རྟོགས" uses the adverbial "མེད་པར" (with/as there being none): the bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom in the mode that nothing is afflicted or purified (bo-mipham 5-18: "...ཡང་མེད་པར་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔས ... རྗེས་སུ་རྟོགས་པར་གྱུར"). The English coordinating "And" loses this link.
issues.fix: In this, there being nothing that becomes afflicted or completely pure, the bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.

issues.span: It eclipses all fireflies and all living beings
issues.evidence: The Tibetan "སྲིན་བུ་མེ་ཁྱེར་སྲོག་ཆགས་འབྱུང་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་དང་། སྐར་མའི་ཚོགས་དང་ཟླ་བའི་འོད་ཀུན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན" has the sun overpower the light of fireflies and creatures, stars and moon ("འོད་ཀུན" scopes over the list). bo-rangjung 5-25: "སྲིན་བུ་མེ་ཁྱེར་དང་སྲོག་ཆགས་འབྱུང་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་འོད་དང༌། ... ཟླ་བའི་འོད་ཀུན་ཀྱང་ཉི་མའི་འོད་ཀྱིས་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན"; bo-khenrab 5-25 likewise speaks of the light of creatures with a little light. The English says the beings themselves are eclipsed.
issues.fix: It eclipses the light of all fireflies and all (light-bearing) living creatures, along with the hosts of stars and all the light of the moon

issues.span: desires the purpose of giving away wealth
issues.evidence: "ནོར་གཏོང་དོན་འདོད་པ": bo-mipham 5-27 explains that the prince gives away wealth to take care of his subjects and wishes ("དོན༷་འདོ༷ད་པ") to protect the realm for their benefit; the giving is the means to a beneficial aim, not itself the aim. The English reads as unclear.
issues.fix: who desires to benefit others and gives away wealth to do so

issues.span: obtains skillful means
issues.evidence: "ཐབས་ཐོབ་གྱུར་ཏེ": bo-mipham 5-27 glosses it as "རྒྱལ་ས་ལ་དབང་བའི་ཐབས༷་ཐོབ༷་པར་གྱུར༷་ཏེ" (obtaining the means to rule the realm by consecration), and bo-khenrab 5-27 "རྒྱལ་སྲིད་ཀྱི་ཐབས་ཐོབ". In the simile ཐབས is the means of sovereignty, so the locked rendering 'skillful means' gives a misleading sense here (bo-rangjung applies skillful means only to the bodhisattva in the application).
issues.fix: obtains the means of rule (consecration) and is established in the kingdom

issues.span: Buddhas touch awakening through the perfection of patience; Generating mindfulness, thinking, "This mind is not good," They confess and restrain themselves in the future,
issues.evidence: The Tibetan states the Buddhas' attainment as the premise ("སངས་རྒྱས་བཟོད་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པས་བྱང་ཆུབ་རེག"); the one who generates mindfulness, confesses and restrains is the practitioner, who "trains in this Buddha-dharma" ("དེ་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཆོས་འདིར་སློབ"). bo-mipham 5-34: Buddhas touch awakening by patience, so (one who thinks) "this angry mind of mine is not good" generates the mindfulness, confesses and restrains; bo-khenrab 5-34 same. The English participial "Generating mindfulness..." attaches to the Buddhas, making them the ones who confess.
issues.fix: Since Buddhas touch awakening through the perfection of patience, whoever generates mindfulness, thinking "This mind is not good," confesses and also restrains themselves in future,

issues.span: do not rejoice in it
issues.evidence: "དགའ་བར་མི་བྱེད" has no stated object; bo-mipham 5-34 and bo-khenrab 5-34 specify the angry state and quarrelling ("རྩོད་པ་སོགས་ཀྱི་ངང་ཚུལ་ལ་དགའ་བར་མི་བྱེད"), which "it" does not make clear.
issues.fix: do not take pleasure in such anger and quarrelling

issues.span: Which is overpowered by its rays.
issues.evidence: "ཉི་མ་མཁར་ལ་འགྲོ་བའི་ཟེར་གྱིས་ཟིལ་གནོན་པའི། མདུན་གྱི་བར་སྣང": the participle "ཟིལ་གནོན་པའི" qualifies the space ("བར་སྣང") overwhelmed by the sun's rays; bo-khenrab 5-37: "འོད་ཟེར་གྱིས་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་པར་གྱུར་པའི་མདུན་གྱི་བར་སྣང". In the English "Which" can attach to the sun, which would mean the sun is overpowered by its own rays.
issues.fix: Just as darkness does not remain in the space before the sun moving through the sky, space overwhelmed by its rays.

issues.span: If all of them were to take up the intention and become Māras
issues.evidence: "ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་པ་བཟུང་སྟེ་བདུད་གྱུར་ལ" (Skt parikalpa ... bhaveyu māraḥ): a hypothetical supposition ("suppose they all became Māras"). bo-mipham 5-50 introduces it with "དཔེར་ན། གལ་ཏེ་བདུད་དུ་གྱུར་ལ" and bo-khenrab 5-50 "ཡོངས་སུ་བཏག་པ་བཟུང་སྟེ་བདུད་དུ་གྱུར་ལ"; "take up the intention" imports a volitional sense (bo-rangjung's "བསམ་པ") the Tibetan itself does not carry.
issues.fix: If all of them were hypothetically to become Māras

issues.span: in realms equal to the Ganges
issues.evidence: "གང་གཱའི་ཀླུང་མཉམ་ཞིང": the comparison is in number to the grains of sand of the Ganges (Skt gaṅganadivālikasame; bo-mipham 5-50 "རྡུལ་གྱི་གྲངས་དང་མཉམ་པའི་ཞིང"; bo-rangjung 5-50 "བྱེ་མ་སྙེད་དང་མཉམ་པའི་ཞིང"). The English as written says the realms are equal to the river.
issues.fix: in realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges

issues.span: an expounder, one who desires the Dharma, or one who views
issues.evidence: "འཆད་པར་བྱེད་དང་ཆོས་འདོད་ལྟ་བར་བྱེད་མི་དམིགས": bo-mipham 5-54 and bo-khenrab 5-53 read two items, the expounder and the one who desires Dharma, who is regarded as the object of the teaching ("ཆོས་འདོད་མཁན་ཏེ་ཆོས་བཤད་པའི་ཡུལ་ཉིད་དུ་ལྟ་བར་བྱེད་པ"); the Sanskrit likewise has two (deśika, paśyaka). The English makes "one who views" a stand-alone third item with no object.
issues.fix: an expounder, or one who desires the Dharma and views [it as the object of teaching]

issues.span: Knows it to be unborn and unexhausted through this wisdom
issues.evidence: "སྐྱེ་མེད་ཟད་པ་མེད་པར་ཤེས་རབ་འདི་ཤེས་ཏེ": "ཤེས་རབ་འདི" is the object known, not the instrument; bo-mipham 5-64 "ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་དོན་ཟབ་མོ་འདི་ལྟ་བུ་ཤེས་པར་བྱས" (knowing this profound meaning of the perfection of wisdom), with unborn and inexhaustible predicated of dependent origination. The English "through this wisdom" turns the object into a means.
issues.fix: Knows dependent origination to be unborn and inexhaustible, and knows this wisdom,

issues.span: free from the vehicle of the arhat and pratyekabuddha
issues.evidence: The Tibetan དགྲ་བཅོམ་རང་རྒྱལ་ཐེག་བྲལ་ is glossed in bo-mipham 5-74 as ཐེག་པ་འདོད་པ་དང་བྲལ་ (free from the wish for the vehicle of arhats and pratyekabuddhas) and in bo-khenrab 5-74 as འདོད་པ་དང་དོན་གཉེར་གྱི་བློ་དང་བྲལ་; the English could be read as simply not belonging to that vehicle.
issues.fix: free from [the wish for] the vehicle of the arhat and pratyekabuddha

issues.span: even if they intensely engage in them, If they are free
issues.evidence: Lines 2-3 use 'they' with no antecedent; the subject །དཔའ་བོ་ (hero) only appears in line 4, so the conditional clauses are hard to parse.
issues.fix: Even if the hero intensely engages in them, if he is free ... and delights ..., he should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise

issues.span: and they will become wise
issues.evidence: In འགྲོ་བ་དགའ་འགྱུར་མཁས the 'wise' (མཁས) describes the patient one, not the beings. bo-mipham 5-88: བཟོད་པ་དང་ལྡན་པ་དེ་ལ་འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་དགའ་བར་འགྱུར་... རྨོངས་པ་དང་བྲལ་བའི་མཁས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ (the patient one becomes wise, free of ignorance); bo-khenrab 5-88 likewise; bo-rangjung 5-87: འགྲོ་བ་དད་ཅིང་དགའ་བར་འགྱུར་བ་དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཉིད་ཤེས་པས་མཁས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ. Sanskrit: priyu bhoti sarvajagati kṣamamāṇu vijño (dear to all the world, the patient one, wise).
issues.fix: Beings will rejoice in this one endowed with patience, who is wise.

issues.span: This is the purpose of ethical discipline
issues.evidence: Tibetan ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་དོན; bo-mipham 5-95 and bo-khenrab 5-95 read ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་ཀྱི་དོན་དུ་གསུངས / ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་ཀྱི་དོན་ཡིན་པར་གསུངས (this is taught as the meaning of ethical discipline), cf. Sanskrit śīlaartha; 'purpose' shifts the sense to a goal.
issues.fix: This is the meaning of ethical discipline for those endowed with ...

issues.span: enjoying sensory pleasure
issues.evidence: The Tibetan says only འདོད་ཡོན་ལྔ་སྤྱོད་ཀྱང་ (practises/enjoys the five qualities of desire); 'sensory pleasure' is not a separate item and merely restates the object (bo-mipham 5-96: འདོད་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་ལྔ་ལ་ཞེན་པའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་སྤྱོད་པར་གྱུར་ཀྱང་).
issues.fix: delete 'enjoying sensory pleasure'

issues.span: I must become a Buddha
issues.evidence: སངས་རྒྱས་འགྲུབ་བྱ་སྙམ་ is a resolve 'I shall accomplish buddhahood' (bo-mipham 5-96 and bo-khenrab 5-95: བདག་གིས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་གོ་འཕང་འགྲུབ་པར་བྱའོ་སྙམ་; Sanskrit buddho bhaviṣyāmi), not an obligation.
issues.fix: "I shall accomplish buddhahood"

issues.span: properly seek to be a śrāvaka
issues.evidence: ཉན་ཐོས་ལེགས་ཚོལ་ is glossed in bo-mipham 5-107 as དེའི་འབྲས་བུ་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ལེགས་པར་ཚོལ་བ (earnestly seek the śrāvaka awakening as the result of the gifts) and in bo-rangjung 5-106 as འབྲས་བུ་ཉན་ཐོས་ཚོལ་ན; Sanskrit śrāvakaguṇān; the object sought is the śrāvaka's fruit, not simply being a śrāvaka.
issues.fix: earnestly seek the awakening of a śrāvaka as the result

issues.span: Who rejoices in their basis of meritorious action
issues.evidence: དེ་དག་བསོད་ནམས་བྱ་བའི་དངོས་ལ་ཡི་རང་ནས: དེ་དག (those) refers back to the beings giving gifts in 5-107, not to the bodhisattva. bo-mipham 5-107: བཤད་མ་ཐག་པ་དེ་དག་གི་བསོད་ནམས་བྱ་བའི་དངོས་པོ་དེ་ལ་ཡི་རང་བར་བྱས་ནས; bo-rangjung 5-108: འཁོར་འདས་དེ་དག་གི་བསོད་ནམས་བྱ་བའི་དངོས་པོ་ལ་ཡིད་རང་ནས; Sanskrit teṣāṃ puṇyakriyāvastu. In the English 'their' can only be read as the bodhisattva's own basis, reversing whose merit is rejoiced in.
issues.fix: Who rejoices in those [beings'] bases of meritorious action
